_note: Supply chain traces, ordered from the reactor back to the mine. 'stages' are shared by every route; 'routes' split the chain where there is more than one source. A lens annotation of null renders as 'Not yet researched for this lens'. sourceNeeded:true renders a visible 'Source needed' flag. 'rating' drives node colour only: supply = supply risk (security lens), harm = harm severity (people lens). Values: high | moderate | low | unknown. Ratings are the author's judgement and should be reviewed.

documented.label: Documented
documented.meaning: Credible public evidence (NGO, UN, government, peer-reviewed) of human rights harm at this stage

likely.label: Likely pathway
likely.meaning: Harm at the source is documented; the link from that source into fusion's supply chain is plausible by market structure but not proven

hypothesis.label: Hypothesis
hypothesis.meaning: A link worth testing; no direct evidence yet

yttrium.name: Yttrium
yttrium.role: The rare earth in REBCO superconducting tape

whyItMatters.text: Compact tokamaks use high-temperature superconducting magnets made from REBCO tape ("rare-earth barium copper oxide"). Faraday Factory's tape uses yttrium as the rare earth; Fujikura's uses gadolinium or europium. Both put a yttrium-oxide buffer layer under the superconductor, so yttrium is in the tape either way.

stages.name: Compact tokamak developers (e.g. Commonwealth Fusion Systems)

security.text: Compact tokamak developers depend on HTS tape. CFS buys from Fujikura (an order for over 10,000 km in 2026) and Faraday Factory Japan. Russian customs records also show coated Hastelloy tape (oxide, silver and copper layers) exported from Moscow to CFS in January–April 2022.

people.text: Buyers sit several tiers removed from the mine. We found no public human rights traceability for magnet materials from fusion developers or tape makers; industry supply-chain reports (DOE, FIA) do not address it.

sayari.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems LLC
sayari.basis: Russian customs: 9 export records of coated Hastelloy C276 tape from S-Innovations to CFS, Jan–Apr 2022.

security.text: A small number of makers supply fusion: Fujikura and Faraday Factory Japan (CFS), and Faraday Factory (Proxima Fusion). Sayari shows Faraday Factory Japan importing coated Hastelloy tape from Moscow until January 2025. Some is described with a yttrium-oxide buffer and some with barium-copper-yttrium oxide and silver layers, which is the superconducting layer itself.

people.text: Sayari shows no yttrium oxide or yttrium targets reaching any tape maker. Its Japanese import records (from 2023) show Faraday Factory Japan receiving tape from Moscow, but no rare earth shipments to Fujikura or Faraday Factory. Coverage is partial, so the absence is not proof.

sayari.name: Fujikura Ltd.
sayari.role: Tape maker; CFS's main supplier for ARC
sayari.basis: No HTS tape or yttrium shipments recorded.
sayari.watchlist: Not sanctioned. Group-level modelled flags come from its wider cable trade, not HTS tape.

sayari.name: Faraday Factory Japan LLC
sayari.role: Tape maker; supplies CFS and Proxima Fusion
sayari.basis: 369 shipments received from Russia, Feb 2023 – Jan 2025 (Russian export and Japanese import records): 261 from S-Innovations, 106 from a same-address duplicate record. Descriptions include 'Hastelloy C276 alloy tape with Mg, Cu, Ba, Y oxide layers and a silver surface layer'.

sayari.role: Moscow tape maker in the SuperOx group
sayari.basis: Exported coated tape to CFS (2022) and to Faraday Factory Japan (2023–25). INN 5032242530.
sayari.watchlist: Not sanctioned. Flags: imports_bis_high_priority_items, meu_list_contractors, sanctioned_adjacent (modelled adjacency).

security.text: China added yttrium to export licensing on 4 April 2025. Chinese customs data show yttrium exports to the US fell to 17 tonnes in April–December 2025, from 333 tonnes in the eight months before.

stages.name: Heavy rare earth separation, China (and Lynas, Malaysia)

security.text: Separation of heavy rare earths, including yttrium, is overwhelmingly in China: about 99% until 2023. Sayari records Fujian separators shipping consignments described as yttrium oxide to Japanese importers in 2022–23. Lynas (Malaysia), the main non-Chinese separator, ships mostly light rare earths, largely to Japan. None is recorded selling to a tape maker.

people.text: Ore from Myanmar enters Chinese separation plants and leaves as Chinese product. Origin is lost here.

sayari.name: Fujian Changting Golden Dragon Rare Earth
sayari.basis: Shipments described as 'yttrium oxide' to Japanese importers (Tokuyo International Logistics, Daiichi Kigenso Kagaku Kogyo), 2022–23.

sayari.name: Ganzhou Chenguang Rare Earths New Material
sayari.basis: Rare earth compounds (HS 284690) to Shinwa Bussan, Japan, 2022-04; product not specified beyond the HS heading.

sayari.name: Lynas Malaysia Sdn Bhd
sayari.basis: 934 HS 284690 shipments 2019–2026, 445 to Japan (mostly Sojitz); products recorded are light rare earths (cerium, NdPr).
sayari.watchlist: Not sanctioned. Its forced-labour and SOE flags are modelled sub-tier indicators, not findings about its operations.

stages.name: Kachin State, Myanmar

security.text: Myanmar produced a significant share of world yttrium supply in 2025, according to USGS, from ionic-clay heavy rare earth mines in Kachin State.

people.text: 300+ mining sites in Kachin Special Region 1 (40%+ growth 2021–23), run until late 2024 by a junta-aligned militia and since then under the Kachin Independence Army. Streams are acidic and arsenic-contaminated. Workers, including children, have died after chemical exposure, and landslides killed at least 35 miners in June 2024. Workers report physical violence and sexual exploitation, and opponents of mining face arrests and threats. The trade risks financing conflict.

stages.evidenceNote: Published investigations focus on dysprosium and terbium; yttrium-specific tracing to tape was not found. Sayari holds no Myanmar-to-China rare earth trade records, so this stage rests on NGO and press sources.

harm.extremeBasis: S1: a 15-year-old boy among miners who died; S3: deaths of mine workers including children; workers report physical violence and sexual exploitation.
harm.reason: Rated severe: child labour, violence against workers and sexual exploitation documented (5 sources).

security.text: China produced most of the world's yttrium in 2025 (USGS), largely from ionic clays in southern provinces such as Jiangxi and Fujian.

people.text: Severe environmental damage from heavy rare earth mining in Jiangxi: Chinese authorities put the cleanup at about US$5.6 billion, with 50–100 years to recover.

harm.reason: Rated moderate: harm documented by 1 source.

yttrium.bottomLine: The magnets at the heart of compact fusion depend on yttrium separated overwhelmingly in China, where ore from armed-group-controlled Kachin State is mixed in and its origin lost. Sayari confirms who makes the tape and that part of it ran through Moscow until 2025, but no record shows where any tape maker's yttrium comes from. Harm at Kachin is documented; the link into fusion magnets is likely, not proven.

nickel.name: Nickel
nickel.role: The alloy backing (Hastelloy C-276) that REBCO tape is built on

whyItMatters.text: REBCO tape is built on thin strip of Hastelloy C-276, a nickel-chromium-molybdenum alloy. Specialty mills market this strip directly to tape makers.

security.text: CFS buys tape from Faraday Factory Japan and Fujikura. Russian customs records in Sayari show two flows between CFS and Moscow's S-Innovations group. Coated Hastelloy tape went to CFS in January–April 2022 (9 records). Uncoated Hastelloy C-276 tape went from CFS to Moscow from May 2022 to December 2024 (15 records, about 29 tonnes; about US$5 million where values are declared). Early shipments were declared 'for own use for research purposes'; later ones carry no such statement.

sayari.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems LLC
sayari.role: Recorded shipper of Hastelloy C276 tape to Moscow
sayari.basis: Russian customs: 15 HS 750620 imports from CFS, 2022-05-04 to 2024-12-17 (11 by S-Innovations, 4 by SuperOx-Innovations; the two December 2024 rows may be one shipment recorded twice); 9 exports of coated tape from S-Innovations to CFS, 2022-01 to 2022-04.

security.text: A major REBCO tape supplier to fusion developers. Russian export and Japanese import records show it received 369 shipments from Moscow between February 2023 and January 2025. 327 were Hastelloy C-276 tape, ranging from bare polished strip to strip already carrying the oxide buffer, the yttrium-barium-copper oxide superconductor and a silver layer.

sayari.name: Faraday Factory Japan LLC
sayari.basis: 369 shipments received from Russia, Feb 2023 – Jan 2025 (201 Russian export and 168 Japanese import records, so some may be counted twice).

security.text: A Moscow company in the SuperOx group, which published fusion-tape research with CFS, makes buffered and superconducting-coated Hastelloy tape and ships it to Faraday Factory Japan. It buys the bare alloy tape from CFS and from Chinese mills and traders. Sayari flags it for importing items on the US BIS high-priority list; it is not itself sanctioned.

sayari.name: OOO S-Innovatsii (S-Innovations LLC)
sayari.role: Coats Hastelloy tape; ships it to Faraday Factory Japan
sayari.basis: INN 5032242530; same tax ID as SuperOx-Innovations.
sayari.watchlist: Not sanctioned. Flags: imports_bis_high_priority_items, meu_list_contractors, sanctioned_adjacent (modelled adjacency).

sayari.name: OOO SuperOx-Innovatsii
sayari.role: Same operation, recorded under a second name
sayari.basis: 77 received shipments, including 4 from CFS (2023).

security.text: VDM Metals (Germany) and Elgiloy (US) market C-276 strip as tape substrate. Russian import records show Chinese mills also supplying it.

people.text: Nickel from many mines is melted together here. Sayari shows no Indonesian supplier upstream of Haynes International or VDM, and the Chinese mills have no upstream data at all.

sayari.name: Haynes International Inc
sayari.basis: 39 recorded trade partners; none Indonesian.

sayari.name: VDM Metals International GmbH
sayari.basis: Nickel-filtered upstream supply chain: 0 results.

sayari.name: Jiangsu Rylision Steel Co Ltd
sayari.basis: 1 shipment (2022-09), described as substrate for thin-film deposition. Upstream: 0 results.

people.text: Indonesia's human rights commission (Komnas HAM, 2026) found the state failed to protect rights around Morowali, where respiratory infections are rising. A furnace explosion at a Morowali smelter killed 21 workers in December 2023. At Weda Bay, companies working with police and military have taken land from Indigenous communities through coercion and intimidation, and rivers are polluted with hexavalent chromium.

evidence.scope: link to fusion: no Sayari path found

sayari.name: Indonesia Morowali Industrial Park
sayari.basis: Resolved only; no link to the substrate chain found.

harm.reason: Rated severe: harm documented by 3 sources.

nickel.bottomLine: Sayari did not confirm the Indonesia hypothesis: no path links tape substrate to Morowali or Weda Bay. It found a different route instead. Hastelloy tape from the US and China is coated in Moscow and shipped to a Japanese maker that supplies fusion developers.

tin.name: Tin

security.text: ITER's toroidal-field coils used more than 500 t of Nb₃Sn strand, made in 2008–2015 by eight suppliers working for six ITER members.

ITER's strand came from Bruker EAS (Germany), Bruker OST (US), JASTEC and SH Copper (Japan), Kiswire Advanced Technology (South Korea), Luvata, Western Superconducting Technologies (China) and Chepetsky Mechanical Plant (Russia). Chepetsky has been on Ukraine's NSDC sanctions list since October 2022 (not the US, EU or UK lists) and records Western Superconducting as owned by a Chinese state-owned enterprise.

people.text: Sayari holds no niobium or tin shipments into any of these strand makers, so where their metal comes from cannot be traced from trade data.

evidence.scope: where their tin and niobium come from

routes.name: Man Maw, Wa State → Yunnan smelters

security.text: Wa State has no smelters; ore goes to smelters in Yunnan, China. The largest, Yunnan Tin, is state-owned according to Sayari's registry data.

people.text: Origin is lost at smelting. Sayari holds no Myanmar-to-China tin ore records, so this flow cannot be shown from trade data.

sayari.name: Yunnan Tin Co., Ltd.
sayari.basis: Registry: USCC 915300007134002589. No Myanmar ore receipts recorded.
sayari.watchlist: Owned by a Chinese state-owned enterprise; regulatory_action flag.

security.text: At its peak Myanmar was the world's 3rd-largest tin producer, nearly all of it from Man Maw. The mine was suspended in 2023 and began a slow restart in 2025–26, with output still well below earlier levels.

people.text: Controlled by the United Wa State Army, an armed group under US sanctions since 2003 for narcotics trafficking and listed by the UN Secretary-General for recruiting and using children. A 2022 explosion at the mine killed nine workers.

sayari.name: United Wa State Army
sayari.role: Armed group controlling the Man Maw area
sayari.basis: Its Sayari network holds sanctioned individuals and Hong Pang companies; no tin traders or smelters.
sayari.watchlist: On the US OFAC sanctions list (SDN 7825).

types: child recruitment by the controlling armed group
harm.note: The UN child-recruitment listing concerns the armed group, not the mine itself, so it is not used as the extreme-harm trigger; the stage is severe on source count.
harm.reason: Rated severe: harm documented by 3 sources.

routes.name: Great Lakes traders → Malaysia Smelting Corp

security.text: A second tin smelting hub. It buys tin concentrate shipped from Tanzania, Rwanda, the DRC and Burundi by international traders, plus one lot from Myeik, southern Myanmar (November 2025). Its suppliers include Star Dragon Corporation, a Hong Kong trader the US sanctioned in August 2025 for buying minerals from a Rubaya mining company linked to an armed group. Star Dragon shipped 10 lots of tin ore to the smelter between September 2024 and August 2025, mostly from the DRC.

people.text: Origin is lost at smelting. Shipping records name countries, not mines. Some lots are declared as Congolese-origin tin, and others leave from Rwanda, where the UN says smuggled Congolese minerals are mixed into exports.

sayari.name: Malaysia Smelting Corporation Bhd
sayari.basis: 38 rows of HS 2609 tin concentrate from Tanzania (2025–26), 28 from Rwanda, 12 from the DRC, 1 from Myeik, Myanmar (2025-11-27).
sayari.watchlist: Not sanctioned. Directly supplied by an OFAC-listed trader (Star Dragon).

sayari.name: Star Dragon Corporation Limited
sayari.role: Hong Kong trader; direct supplier of tin ore to the smelter
sayari.basis: 10 HS 2609 tin ore and concentrate shipments to Malaysia Smelting Corp, Sep 2024 – 14 Aug 2025, mostly departing the DRC.
sayari.watchlist: On the US OFAC sanctions list (SDN 55049) since 12 Aug 2025, for supporting a company selling Rubaya minerals from armed-group-controlled areas.

types: conflict financing via a sanctioned supplier

people.text: Four traders shipping tin concentrate to the smelter (Traxys Europe, GM Trading, Halcyon and Sizer Metals) also buy coltan from Rwandan exporters that Global Witness says bought conflict coltan from Rubaya. The records do not show that conflict-linked ore reached the smelter.

sayari.basis: 17 HS 2615 coltan shipments from Rwanda; HS 2609 tin concentrate to Malaysia Smelting Corp (2025-11).

sayari.name: GM Trading Co., Ltd.

sayari.basis: Buys from African Panther and Boss Mining (Rwanda); tin concentrate to the smelter (2025-11, 2026-02).

sayari.name: Sizer Metals Pte Ltd
sayari.basis: Buys from African Panther (Rwanda); tin concentrate to the smelter (2025-11).

harm.reason: Rated moderate: harm documented by 1 source.

context.label: Sector-wide
context.text: Verisk Maplecroft (2017) rated tin the highest-risk of the 3TG minerals for labour rights violations, and rated child labour an "extreme risk" in Bolivia, Myanmar and Indonesia.

tin.bottomLine: Fusion's Nb₃Sn strand makers are known, but Sayari shows no tin going into any of them. Upstream, Myanmar tin from a mine run by a US-sanctioned armed group disappears into Chinese smelters, and a second smelter in Malaysia buys from traders who also handle Rwanda's conflict-linked coltan. The harm is documented; the route into fusion is not traced.

people.text: Coltan (which yields tantalum and niobium) from M23-occupied Rubaya is smuggled to Rwanda and mixed with Rwandan production (UN Group of Experts, 2025). Smelters that processed it still passed industry audits. Amnesty International documented M23 forcing miners to work, torturing them, and killing at least 18 miners at Rubaya and a nearby gold mine. The armed group that held Rubaya before M23 also used forced labour and executed civilians, according to the US Treasury. Tunnel collapses in 2026 killed hundreds of miners.

harm.extremeBasis: Amnesty International (2026): M23 forced miners to dig, tortured them and killed at least 18 miners; US Treasury: PARECO-FF used forced labour and executed civilians.
harm.reason: Rated severe: forced labour, killings and torture documented (5 sources).

niobium.bottomLine: About 93% of niobium comes from Brazil. A small stream from M23-occupied Rubaya is laundered through Rwanda; Sayari confirms the exporters and the traders who buy from them, but shows no niobium entering any strand maker. A fusion link remains a hypothesis.

tungsten.name: Tungsten
tungsten.role: Plasma-facing armour for the divertor and first wall

security.text: Only a few firms make fusion-grade tungsten parts. A.L.M.T. (Sumitomo, Japan) holds an ITER contract for tungsten monoblocks and also supplies Europe's ITER divertor targets. State-owned AT&M (China) says it made divertor parts for France's WEST and China's EAST. Plansee (Austria) made test divertor pieces for Europe's ITER agency, but no production contract was found.

sayari.basis: Upstream supply chain: 0 suppliers recorded.

sayari.name: Advanced Technology & Materials Co. (AT&M)
sayari.role: Divertor parts for WEST and EAST

security.text: Plansee says it sources tungsten from scrap recycling and long-term mine off-take deals, including the Sangdong mine in South Korea.

people.text: Shipment records show this powder plant buying tungsten concentrate from Colombian exporters (2012–13) and from the trader Traxys (2026). Traxys also buys Rwandan tungsten ore. Nothing shows that Rwandan lots reached this plant, or that its tungsten went into a fusion part.

people.text: Tungsten is one of the 3TG "conflict minerals". Armed groups such as the ELN have controlled some tungsten mining in Colombia (Verisk Maplecroft, 2017; ICIJ). Sayari records Rwandan and Colombian ore exports to traders and powder makers, but not conditions at those mines.

tungsten.bottomLine: Only a handful of firms make fusion-grade tungsten, and China mines about four-fifths of the world's supply. Sayari shows a Western powder maker buying ore through a trader that also handles Rwandan tungsten, but nothing ties conflict-linked ore to a fusion part.

steel.name: Specialty steels

stages.name: EUROFER97 low-activation steel (blanket structures): Saarschmiede, Böhler

security.text: Europe's reference fusion steel, EUROFER97, has so far been made industrially by two firms. F4E's 2015 order of 27 t was forged by Saarschmiede (Germany) with Böhler (Austria) as subcontractor.

people.text: No human rights hotspot identified at this stage. Alloying inputs, including about 1% tungsten, were not traced.

sayari.name: Saarschmiede GmbH Freiformschmiede
sayari.basis: Registry: HRB 75004.

steel.bottomLine: Shown for contrast: a real bottleneck for building reactors, but not a human rights hotspot on current research. Its tungsten content links it back to the tungsten chain.
